title: Structures and dynamics of the major G-quadruplex in the human PDGFR-beta gene promoter: insights into vacancy G-quadruplex formation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded PDB entry 9P9X (598 KB plain-text coordinate file): it is a 10-model NMR (nuclear magnetic resonance) ensemble of ONE 22-nucleotide DNA strand, sequence AAGGGAGGGCGGCGGGGCAGGG, title 'Solution structure of the major PDGFRB promoter G-quadruplex with a broken-strand G22 fill-in'. Listed the supplement via Europe PMC: 17 files, of which the only non-figure item is an 8.5 MB PDF of NMR spectra; no CSV, TSV or XLSX table anywhere. Confirmed 9P9Y and BMRB (Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank) entries 31252/31253 are the only other deposits named in the data availability statement.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That 9P9Y is the shorter Pu21 construct and that the two conformations interconvert on a millisecond timescale with an exchange rate fitted from NOESY (nuclear Overhauser effect spectroscopy) peak buildup; I did not open 9P9Y or the BMRB chemical-shift files because the row count was already fatal.

a1_downloadable.note: Protein Data Bank entries 9P9X/9P9Y and BMRB 31252/31253 are fully open; I downloaded 9P9X without any login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table at all. Any prediction target (fold topology, which guanine fills the vacancy, exchange rate) would have to be constructed by hand from 3D coordinates and NMR spectra figures in a PDF.

a3_inputs_present.note: The DNA sequence is present in the SEQRES records of the coordinate file, so inputs need no lookup — but there are only two of them.

a4_units_stated.note: Coordinates are in angstroms per PDB format; buffer conditions (10-100 mM potassium phosphate/KCl, pH 7.0) and the exchange rate units are stated in the methods.

a5_enough_rows.note: FATAL. The paper deposits two structures of two closely related oligonucleotides (Pu22, 22 nt; Pu21, 21 nt) from the same promoter. Two labelled items against a threshold of ~400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Two PDB coordinate files plus two chemical-shift tables; trivially small.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The paper claims two interconverting conformations and two PDB depositions; I found exactly two accessions, and 9P9X matches the described 22-mer.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would be experimental NMR-derived structures, not another model's output — provenance is clean, there is simply almost none of it.

existing_models.name: G4ShapePredictor (G4SP), gradient-boosted tree classifiers for G-quadruplex fold topology from sequence, Scientific Reports 2024
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on 1,005 sequence-topology pairs assembled from literature plus in-house circular dichroism; reported accuracy not retrieved (search snippet only, paper not opened).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Snippet states no prior model predicted G-quadruplex folding topology from sequence; I did not open the discussion so I cannot quote their named open problem.

existing_models.name: G4detector / PENGUINN / DeepG4 / G4mismatch / G4-Attention, convolutional and attention neural networks predicting G-quadruplex formation from sequence using G4-seq data
existing_models.score_and_split: G4-Attention reports area under the ROC curve of 0.999 against a putative-quadruplex negative set; benchmarked against G4detector, G4Hunter, pqsfinder and Quadron (search snippets, papers not opened).

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 or Nucleotide Transformer (DNA language models with open weights)
backbone.licence: Permissive to non-commercial depending on checkpoint

integration.partner_dataset: G4ShapePredictor's 1,005 sequence-topology pairs, or all ~5,019 full-text 'G-quadruplex' hits in the Protein Data Bank
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Can sequence predict which guanines fill a vacancy G-quadruplex? — but this paper contributes 2 of the thousands of rows such a study would need, so it is a citation, not a dataset.

controls.external_validation: Other G-quadruplex NMR structures in the PDB would be the external set, but then this paper is not the dataset.

honest_claim_h3: No model can be trained on this paper's data; the honest claim is limited to 'the PDGFR-beta promoter Pu22 and Pu21 sequences adopt these two specific broken-strand folds in potassium buffer at pH 7.0'.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a promoter DNA sequence to predict which four-stranded guanine fold it adopts and which guanine fills the gap.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need thousands of DNA sequences each labelled with an experimentally determined four-stranded (G-quadruplex) fold; this paper supplies 2 sequences, verified by opening the coordinate file.
plain_idea.predict: The fold class and, for gapped folds, which guanine plugs the vacancy. Truth comes from solution NMR structure determination, which takes months of spectrometer time per sequence.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Medicinal chemists designing small molecules that lock G-quadruplexes shut to silence cancer-driving genes would use a sequence-to-fold predictor; but that project needs a pooled multi-paper structure set, not this one paper.

more_or_better_data.why: Two structures versus G4ShapePredictor's 1,005 sequence-topology pairs and the G4-seq genome-wide datasets behind G4detector and G4-Attention.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements and no per-group counts; with two items there is nothing from which to estimate uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: Irrelevant here — we have no training data to beat them with. G4-Attention is a 2025-era attention model reporting area under the ROC curve near 0.999 on its own benchmark.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: our model cannot see everything the baseline sees, because this paper provides 2 rows rather than a dataset.

ml_idea: Considered: predict G-quadruplex folding topology and vacancy fill-in from promoter sequence using a DNA language model with a frozen backbone and a small classification head. Dead on arrival for this paper because the deposited data is two oligonucleotide structures; the idea belongs to a pooled PDB-wide G-quadruplex structure set, where G4ShapePredictor already sits.

effort.compute_note: Sizes read directly from the downloaded 598 KB PDB file and the Europe PMC supplement listing; nothing timed because there is no model to train.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the depositions in the data availability statement: two PDB entries and two BMRB entries, i.e. two DNA sequences. Took one minute and killed it.

verdict_reason: A5 and A2 both fail outright: the paper's complete dataset is two NMR structures of two 21-22 nucleotide DNA strands from one promoter, with no tabular supplement (the only non-figure file is an 8.5 MB PDF of spectra), so there is no feature/label table and nothing approaching the ~400-row floor. This is a high-quality structural biology paper whose data belongs in a pooled G-quadruplex structure collection, not a standalone ML project.
